Amplitud, frecuencia, fase y desplazamie: Amplitude, frequency, phase and shift are the four controls of almost everything that repeats. In a sound, the amplitude is the volume and the frequency is how low or high it sounds; in light, the frequency is the colour. An equaliser manipulates amplitudes; the volume knob moves just one of those letters. And tides, the hours of sunshine through the year or a city's electricity consumption are modelled with these same four figures.

Los senos tienen un uso moderno que sorp: Sines have a modern use that comes as a surprise. Language models process all the words at once and, as they stand, would not tell the order apart: “the dog bites the man” and “the man bites the dog” would look the same to them. To fix it, each word has added to it a fingerprint built from sines and cosines of different frequencies — the fast ones tell neighbouring positions apart and the slow ones place the word in the text as a whole — chosen so that the same separation between two words always gives the same similarity, wherever the sentence is. It is in [[ia-atencion|the topic on attention]].

Que cualquier vibración se pueda descomp: That any vibration can be broken down into sines was guessed by Daniel Bernoulli in 1753 while studying vibrating strings, and the idea caused one of the great rows of the eighteenth century: Euler and d'Alembert maintained that it could not be true for functions with corners. Bernoulli was right and could not prove it. The proof came with Fourier, half a century later, and his was rejected at first too.
Queda una pregunta que este tema no cont: One question this topic does not answer remains: where do waves come from? Nobody draws them by hand; they appear on their own the moment something has a force pulling it back to equilibrium in proportion to how far away it is. That sentence is an equation — $x'' = -kx$ — and its solution is exactly these sines. It is in [[av-oscilador|the second-order equation]], and it explains the pendulum, the spring, the radio circuit and the shaking of a bridge.

Sumar ondas explica dos cosas que se oye: Adding waves explains two things you can hear. One is the beat: two almost equal notes produce a slow throb, and that is exactly what a piano tuner listens for — when the throb disappears, the string is in tune. The other is noise-cancelling headphones, which record the sound outside and emit that same wave inverted so that the sum cancels. Silence built out of addition.
